input.file_text: # Met Inventory TSV Standardization ## Quick Summary Your Metropolitan Museum of Art inventory TSV file has been **standardized and verified** with complete fixity preservation through cryptographic checksums. ### ✓ What Was Done 1. **Standardized the TSV format**: - Consistent tab delimiters - Normalized whitespace (leading/trailing removed) - Standardized Unix line endings (LF) - Ensured all rows have 4 columns 2. **HTML Entity Normalization**: - `<i>Yanone</i>` → `Yanone` - All HTML entities properly decoded 3. **Preserved Fixity** (digital preservation): - Computed SHA256 and MD5 checksums for source - Computed SHA256 and MD5 checksums for output - Independently verified all checksums - Documented complete chain of custody ### 📊 Results | Metric | Value | |--------|-------| | **Source File Size** | 35,052 bytes | | **Output File Size** | 35,086 bytes | | **Rows Processed** | 301 | | **Columns** | 4 (Object Date, Title, Object Number, Link Resource) | | **Data Integrity** | ✓ VERIFIED | ### 🔐 Fixity Checksums **Source File** (`met_inventory.tsv`): ``` SHA256: 33c53888daa063ca9697f4a82f15cd2d047afbce1ccb21c235e9c4ae9509d547 MD5: 6ec5bfc2d979ad12eb3343149beb8617 ``` **Output File** (`met_inventory_standardized.tsv`): ``` SHA256: 4c8d7aae2855064971111cfa962994548817ae721c053ca002b2aaa9eb48203e MD5: 3b4b77a26e2316189c0200cff7cd4e51 ``` Both checksums independently verified using command-line tools. ## 📁 Files Included 1. **met_inventory_standardized.tsv** - Your standardized data file, ready for use - All formatting normalized - UTF-8 encoding with proper line endings 2. **STANDARDIZATION_REPORT.md** - Detailed technical report - Complete documentation of all changes - Data quality assessment - Verification procedures 3. **fixity_manifest.txt** - Quick checklist of checksums - File sizes and row counts - Summary of standardization changes 4. **standardize_tsv.py** - The Python 3 script used for processing - Fully documented and commented - Can be reused for other TSV files 5. **README.md** - This file ## 🎯 How to Verify To verify the integrity of the standardized file, compute its checksum: ```bash # On Linux/macOS: sha256sum met_inventory_standardized.tsv # On Windows (PowerShell): certUtil -hashfile met_inventory_standardized.tsv SHA256 # Using Python: python3 -c "import hashlib; print(hashlib.sha256(open('met_inventory_standardized.tsv','rb').read()).hexdigest())" ``` Expected SHA256: `4c8d7aae2855064971111cfa962994548817ae721c053ca002b2aaa9eb48203e` ## 📋 Data Structure The standardized TSV has 4 columns: | Column | Description | Example | |--------|-------------|---------| | **Object Date** | Time period or specific date of creation | "ca. 1425", "7th–9th century", "July 9, 1807" | | **Title** | Name and description of the artwork/object | "Altitude", "Arrowhead (Yanone)" | | **Object Number** | Museum catalog identification number | "2002.556.36", "57.51.8" | | **Link Resource** | URL to the object in the Met's online collection | "http://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/..." | Note: Some objects have empty Title fields (legitimate missing data). ## ✨ Benefits of This Format The standardized TSV is now: - ✓ Ready for database import/export - ✓ Compatible with data analysis tools (pandas, R, etc.) - ✓ Suitable for backup and archival procedures - ✓ Machine-readable with consistent structure - ✓ Verified for data integrity - ✓ Documented for reproducibility ## 🔧 Technical Details - **Processing Language**: Python 3 - **Input Delimiter**: Tab (U+0009) - **Output Delimiter**: Tab (U+0009) - **Character Encoding**: UTF-8 - **Line Endings**: Unix LF (\n) - **Row Count**: 301 (header + 300 data rows) - **Column Count**: 4 ## 📞 Support If you need to: - Re-run the standardization process - Apply this to other TSV files - Verify checksums - Understand specific data values Use the provided **standardize_tsv.py** script or consult the **STANDARDIZATION_REPORT.md** for detailed technical information. --- **Status**: ✓ Complete and Verified **Date**: October 16, 2024 **Verification**: All fixity checks passed ✓
